insights.one_liner: Huge US family-owned food and agriculture group, founded in 1865; its one current Dutch opening is a senior compliance role at Schiphol.

culture.text: A very large, privately held family company; LinkedIn counts about 69,799 staff, Wikidata puts it at 155,000 people in 2022.
Staff mostly studied business, accounting, finance and supply chain, and work mainly in operations, sales, IT and engineering.
Describes itself as sitting at the heart of the food supply chain, from alternative proteins to helping farmers use AI.

open.text: Cargill B.V. and Cargill Bioindustrial B.V. are IND recognised sponsors, so they can sponsor a skilled migrant visa.
Its one open job here (senior, risk and compliance, Schiphol) does not ask for Dutch.
The Dutch entities are owned by Cargill, Incorporated in the US.

growth.text: Revenue was 144.695 billion US dollars in 2018, with net profit of 3.103 billion US dollars.
Earnings fell 52% because of high cattle costs and a cocoa loss.
Is investing 130 million US dollars to expand poultry operations in Thailand and the Philippines.

worth_knowing.text: Recent results were weak: profit was undercut by cattle costs and cocoa losses.
Faces political pressure in the US, with Trump going after Cargill while courting ranchers.
